title: Sample 19-5: Crossword Puzzle

illustrates.quote: l. Insert a transcriber’s note before the crossword puzzle. Sample: In the following crossword puzzle, each clue is followed by a transcriber-assigned column letter and row number. Numbers in parentheses at the end of each clue indicate the number of letters in the puzzle word. The clue letter/number and number of letters in the word are enclosed in transcriber’s note indicators. In the grid, a hyphen represents a square to be filled in, and a full cell represents an empty space.

an 11x11 crossword grid of hyphens (fillable squares) and full cells (blocked squares), column-lettered a-k across the top and row-numbered 1-11 down the side
blocks.features: The grid itself: not braille-buildable in any candidate block type (F-217/219/222).

print.notes: The whole sample spans two braille pages: the transcriber's note (page 1, its own lines 10-20) and, on page 2, the Across/Down clue lists (each with an embedded column/row + letter-count note, per 19.5.2e-g) followed by the crossword grid.
print.printFeatures: Transcriber's note, Across/Down clue lists (each clue with an embedded position/length annotation), and an 11x11 lettered/numbered crossword grid.

braille.notes: Page 1 (source-lines 15406-15416) carries ONLY the transcriber's note, on its own numbered lines 10-20; lines 1-9 are genuinely absent from the source's own extracted text (no numbered braille line exists there at all — the source's own numbering jumps straight from the 'Sample 19-5: Crossword Puzzle' heading to line 10), matching this task's own brief that Sample 19-5's lines 1-9 legitimately lack braille. `lines` below therefore starts directly at the TN (11 lines), then a page break, then page 2 (source-lines 15422-15446, its own line numbering restarting at 1) carrying the Across/Down clue lists and the grid (25 lines).

resolution: Braille re-derived independently from source (source-lines 15406-15416 and 15422-15446, joined with a pageBreaks marker exactly as Sample 19-4 above); differs from both A and B, which had each force-fabricated their own line-count/pageBreaks bookkeeping for the 9 missing lines on page 1 (A: pageBreaks:[14], line count assuming a 14-line first page; B: no pageBreaks at all) without checking that those 9 lines simply have no source content, and are not, e.g., a picture placeholder with an established line count like Sample 19-7's Sudoku. Print side reconciled: the transcriber's note text matches rule 19.5.3l's own quoted 'Sample:' wording verbatim (back-translation-confirmed); the three Across and three Down clues were decoded fresh from the given braille via back-translation and the embedded-note parenthesis decode already established in Example 19-4; the crossword grid remains fully undocumented content (F-217/219/222). Print description corrected 23 Sep 2026 (see printCorrections).
